scope: all MSCI TW index-change names, effective-date closing prints, 2015-2026 (34 events, ~140 name-events)

instances.lock: PRESUMED LIMIT-UP (+9.9% = the 10% cap; OHLC unverifiable — delisted TPEx name)

findings: RARITY IS THE HEADLINE: 3 locked closes in 12 years — 2615 add limit-up and 1789 del limit-down in the 7-percent-limit era (both 2015), OBI Pharma 4174 presumed limit-up Nov-2015 (10 percent era). ZERO locked effective closes 2016-2026: wider limits + anticipated flows + pre-positioned supply (the Step-2 mechanism) have made the classic lock nearly extinct for TW index names

The n=3 outcomes (anecdotes, not statistics, and pinned as such): locked-up ADD 2615 REVERSED (T+1 -2.0, T+2 -3.3 — buyers stuck at the lock got better prices next day); locked-down DEL 1789 bounced mildly then drifted (+1.1/-2.3); mania ADD 4174 CONTINUED (+6.2/+3.6)

THE MODERN VARIANT: 2324 Compal May-2026 — a DELETION that closed +9.6 percent UP on its own deletion day (not locked: high 36.85 vs close 36.70) and ran +9.9/+20.8 after: the crowding SQUEEZE has replaced the lock as the tail risk. For agency client sells the squeeze is a GIFT (better exit); for a guaranteed-close desk pre-hedged short, it is the loss scenario — which is why the compound crowding signature (H16) is the risk flag that matters now
Desk implication: the limit-move playbook stays (locks still possible on corporate-event days and thin TPEx names) but the live monitoring priority is the squeeze signature, not the lock
